in_hebrew.name: איסידורוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם איסידורוס נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'איסיס' (θεα) ו- 'דורוס' (δωρος), שפירושן מתנה של איסיס. איסיס היא אלת הפוריות והקסם במיתולוגיה המצרית, והשם איסידורוס משויך לחזק ואדיר, כמתנה אלוהית. השם משקף את המורשת היוונית והנוצרית כאחד, ומופיע בקרב קהילות נוצריות ברחבי העולם.

in_greek.name: Ισίδωρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ισίδωρος προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'Ισις' (θεα) και 'δωρος' (δωρος), που σημαίνει δωρο της Ισιδας. Η Ισις είναι θεά της γονιμότητας και μαγείας στην αιγύπτιο μυθολογία, και το όνομα Ισίδωρος συνδέεται με την έννοια του ισχυρού και του δαψιλούς, ως δωρο του Θεού. Το όνομα αντανακλά την ελληνική και χριστιανική κληρονομιά και απαντάται σε χριστιανικές κοινότητες παγκοσμίως.

in_latin.name: Isidorus
in_latin.meaning: Gift of Isis, strong and generous
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Isidorus is derived from the Greek words 'Isis' (θεα) and 'doros' (δωρος), meaning gift of Isis. Isis is the Egyptian goddess of fertility and magic, and the name Isidorus connotes strength and generosity, as a divine gift. The name reflects both Greek and Christian heritage, and is found among Christian communities worldwide.

in_english.name: Isidore
in_english.meaning: Gift of Isis, strong and generous
in_english.long_meaning: The name Isidore originates from the Greek words 'Isis' and 'doros', signifying a gift from Isis, the Egyptian goddess of fertility and magic. In Christian tradition, Isidore symbolizes strength, generosity, and divine providence. Historically, the name gained prominence through Saint Isidore of Seville, a revered scholar and theologian of the 7th century. Today, Isidore remains a cherished name across Christian cultures, embodying spiritual richness and intellectual pursuits.

data.cultural_impact: Isidore's name signifies the idea of being a gift from God. In ancient times, children were often named after the circumstances of their birth or significant events, and being named Isidore would have been a way to acknowledge the divine intervention in one's life. Additionally, Saint Isidore is known as the patron saint of farmers, reflecting the importance of agriculturally productive land and stewardship of the earth. In modern times, Isidore has also become the patron saint of students and scholars, a testament to the transformative power of knowledge and education. Moreover, with the increasing digitalization of the world, Isidore has also been adopted as the patron saint of the Internet, reflecting the interconnected web of relationships and information that shapes our world today.
data.spiritual_significance: Isidore's name holds a deep spiritual significance as it reminds us that we are all gifts from God, created with unique strengths and talents that can be used to contribute to the world. In its most fundamental sense, being named Isidore is a call to live a life rooted in faith and gratitude for the divine gift of existence. The name also evokes the idea of stewardship and service, as embodied by the various patronages associated with the saint. As a farmer patron, Isidore invites us to cultivate our own lives and relationships with kindness, patience, and dedication. As a patron of students and scholars, Isidore encourages us to seek knowledge and wisdom as a means of deepening our understanding of the world and ourselves. And as a patron of the Internet, Isidore challenges us to use this powerful tool responsibly, with respect for the interconnected web of relationships and information that makes up the digital world. Ultimately, the name Isidore serves as a reminder of the divine potential within each of us, and the importance of living a life reflecting the gift of God's love.

historical_references.reference: Isidore of Seville (c. 560-636 AD) was a prominent early medieval scholar and bishop of Seville, Spain. He wrote extensively on various subjects including mathematics, astronomy, and theology. His most famous work, the 'Etymologies' or 'Origins', is an encyclopedia of knowledge from a Christian perspective.
historical_references.context: Isidore's works were instrumental in preserving and transmitting classical learning to the Latin West during the early Middle Ages.

historical_references.reference: Saint Isidore of Seville (1050-1130 AD) was a Spanish Roman Catholic priest and a hermit. He is the patron saint of farmers, agricultural workers, and the rural population. His cult became popular in the late Middle Ages, and he is still celebrated in Spain as a protector of crops and livestock.
historical_references.context: Isidore's popularity as a saint was rooted in the agrarian society of medieval Spain, and his association with agriculture and farming continues to this day.

modern_usage.modern_context: Isidore is a common Christian name, originally derived from the Greek word for 'isos' meaning 'equal' and 'doron' meaning 'gift'. In modern context, the name Isidore is associated with figures in technology, education, and encyclopedias. Isidore of Seville, a bishop and scholar from the 6th century, is known for his monumental work, the 'Etymologies', an encyclopedia of all known knowledge at the time. Examples include Isidore Agunbiade, a tech entrepreneur, Isidore Newman School, a renowned educational institution, and Isidore R. Davies, a prominent scholar and contributor to Google Scholar.
